subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support Slack user-level Events API routing and replies as a regular Slack user identity, and what explicit opt-in security boundary is required?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior lets OpenClaw receive and speak as a human Slack account without the normal app identity marker.

options.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a separate Slack mode with authorization matching, send-token binding, allowlist/pairing behavior, docs, and live proof before enabling no-APP-badge replies.

options.title: Keep bot-only ingress
options.body: Document user-level Slack event subscriptions as unsupported and continue requiring users to DM the Slack app/bot identity.

options.title: Prototype outside bundled Slack first
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or fork proof of the user-token event and reply model before deciding whether to promote it into bundled Slack.

recommendation.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a separate Slack mode with authorization matching, send-token binding, allowlist/pairing behavior, docs, and live proof before enabling no-APP-badge replies.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on Slack identity, token, and routing boundaries.
